description: MeitY cites the need for skilled manpower to build blockchain applications as a challenge the NBF/Vishvasya stack is meant to address.
evidence: Launch release says NBF addresses the need for skilled manpower for building blockchain-based applications.

description: Vendor lock-in named by MeitY as a challenge motivating a shared, indigenous, extensible government blockchain stack.
evidence: Launch release lists vendor lock-in among the challenges the framework is designed to tackle.

description: NIC says a lack of trained and experienced blockchain developers was a barrier that led to setting up the CoE.
evidence: NIC blog names lack of trained and experienced developers among barriers prompting the CoE.

description: Lack of investment in blockchain infrastructure and its maintenance cited by NIC as an adoption barrier the CoE was meant to overcome.
evidence: Blog cites lack of investments in infrastructure and its maintenance as a barrier.

description: CoE's multi-node Hyperledger Sawtooth production setup for Drug Logistics chain had node-sync delays, forks and full transaction queues that brought network down.
evidence: Node synchronisation delayed, chain forked, transaction queue filled and network went down; team tried new consensus/Sawtooth releases.

description: PoC had to link GNFC's SAP-based invoicing with the Department of Fertilizers' iFMS; scale-up would need integrating multiple systems of record across the supply chain.
evidence: GNFC invoices sit on SAP servers and are replicated to DoF's iFMS; paper stresses that legacy-system integration must lead design choices.

description: Existing ERP and supply-chain management systems of participants had to be integrated with the blockchain platform to give a unified view of drug movement.
evidence: In the drug track-and-trace implementation, existing ERP/SCM needed integration with the blockchain platform.

description: Blockchain platform could not handle low-latency IoT sensor inputs (e.g., temperature), so a middleware layer filtered events before writing to the ledger.
evidence: A software middle layer passed only significant IoT events to the blockchain, given some platforms' inability to handle low-latency inputs.

description: Supply-chain participants had to adopt a new barcode-scanning step at each transfer, using special three-tier GS1 codes on packaging.
evidence: Stakeholders had to scan barcodes at each stage of transfer, an action not previously required; packaging needed three-tiered QR/barcodes.

description: Officials flagged the need to protect privacy on IndiaChain, e.g., hiding government tender bids and property sale prices on a shared ledger.
evidence: Challenges in safeguarding privacy of individuals and companies; IndiaChain must address identity, privacy and policy.

description: Regulatory and legal framework for IndiaChain was still being drafted when it was announced in Nov 2017.
evidence: Government was still firming up regulations; legal framework pending at time of report.

description: CRDA commissioner said land data must be 'purified' before going on blockchain; wrong data entered becomes permanently encoded.
evidence: Commissioner: whatever data goes on blockchain needs to be purified; garbage in, garbage out.

description: Farmers doubted the private-chain records were safe from officials; citizens could view but not independently verify unauthorised changes, and pre-entry verification remained manipulable.
evidence: Farmers feared officials could change records for bribes; private blockchain gives no independent way to check tampering.

description: Directive makes sanitising (cleaning) revenue records a precondition for securing them on blockchain, implying existing record quality problems.
evidence: CM told officials to ensure revenue records are thoroughly sanitised and secured entirely using blockchain.

description: Revenue, Survey and Registration departments keep land data separately (Webland), causing persistent discrepancies the blockchain platform must reconcile into one record.
evidence: Despite Webland digitisation, discrepancies persisted because Revenue, Survey and Registration departments maintain data separately.

description: Expansion is limited to villages where resurvey and record cleansing are complete; statewide rollout depends on finishing them.
evidence: Villages with completed resurveys to be brought on progressively; statewide rollout targeted from November; grievance cell to find operational shortcomings.

description: Issuing remaining 69 lakh passbooks awaits resurvey of 9,365 villages; CM says revenue records were damaged in 2019–24, requiring digitisation back to 1986.
evidence: 9,365 villages yet to be resurveyed for 69 lakh more passbooks; previous government allegedly damaged revenue records; digitising records from 1986.

description: Officials at the Revenue Dept's Chintan Shibir on adopting AI, blockchain and GIS for land governance flagged data security, privacy safeguards and auditability needs.
evidence: Deliberations stressed data security, privacy safeguards, avoiding algorithmic bias, auditability and human oversight for digital systems.

description: Health data sensitivity meant Print2Block had to rework its product into a private blockchain, with only hashes anchored publicly on Polygon.
evidence: Says healthcare data is very sensitive, so the team tweaked the product and rebuilt a private blockchain.

description: At high volume (14M+ Universal Passes), the service suffered occasional delays and hang-ups.
evidence: Service issued over 14M passes, 'but not without the occasional delay and hang-ups'.

description: Land tokens need legal backing. The state is drafting a DELTA Act, which must fit with the Registration Act, the Transfer of Property Act, stamp duty rules and RERA.
evidence: Tokenisation works only if the token maps to a legally recognised interest; framework must align overlapping property statutes.

description: The CM acknowledged that putting the tokenisation law into practice needs coordination between the Union government, market institutions (SEBI, BSE, NSE) and the state.
evidence: Operationalising the Act would require coordination among Government of India, market institutions and the Maharashtra government.

description: NFT-based land certificates could face legal uncertainty because Finance Bill 2022 broadly defined virtual digital assets; 30% NFT tax could deter land tokenisation.
evidence: EarthID's Sharat Chandra warned the West Bengal initiative might get caught in legal cross-hairs; 30% NFT tax could hinder land tokenisation.

description: Retail e₹ uptake slow: onboarded users and merchants largely inactive, low public awareness of difference from UPI, daily transactions far below RBI's 1-million target.
evidence: Retail CBDC pilot moving slowly; awareness lacking; about 10,000-12,000 daily transactions against a 1-million year-end target (Oct 2023).

description: Usage still low in 2026; report calls for more awareness, usability work and fintech app partnerships.
evidence: IANS (29 May 2026) cites a report saying e-rupee usage is low and needs more awareness, usability and fintech partnerships.

description: Banks' concern about lock-in to a single DLT vendor or platform drove the interoperable multi-platform PoC design (Hyperledger, Corda, Billon).
evidence: Report names vendor lock-in and lack of live at-scale use cases as the main industry concerns motivating the PoC.

description: Cross-platform data transfer between DLT fabrics was seen as risky by most participating banks.
evidence: Data-transfer risk rated high by 18% and medium by 55% of respondents.

description: At go-live many senders, including major banks, had not registered SMS templates on DLT, blocking OTPs and forcing a seven-day suspension of scrubbing.
evidence: Some A2P traffic failed after 8 Mar 2021; all major banks and big telemarketers had not met requirements; scrubbing temporarily suspended.

description: Onboarding about 1.13 lakh principal entities' message chains needed two deadline extensions before traceability could be enforced.
evidence: 1 Nov 2024 traceability deadline extended to 30 Nov, then 10 Dec; undeclared-path messages initially flagged, not blocked.

description: Commentators urged caution: network and device-based blockchain remote voting inherits internet-system vulnerabilities and needs rigorous public appraisal before deployment.
evidence: Editorial summary: system may carry vulnerabilities of any internet-based system; blockchain adds design complexity; ECI should exercise caution.

description: Election Commissioner flagged voter trust: a distributed-consensus voting system must be transparent and understandable to voters.
evidence: Sushil Chandra raised transparency and voter-security concerns; any blockchain solution must be as clear and transparent as possible for voters.

description: Registration does not confer guaranteed title; blockchain-based conclusive titling needs new laws and amendments to TPA, Registration, Stamp, Evidence, IT and data protection Acts.
evidence: SC asked Law Commission to examine Transfer of Property, Registration, Stamp, Evidence, IT and Data Protection Acts for reform.

description: Court warned that inaccurate, incomplete or disputed legacy land records would be carried into a digital version; petitioners said Bihar surveys were incomplete.
evidence: Court warned that if the original record is inaccurate, incomplete or disputed, the digital version will simply perpetuate the flaw.

description: Property registration procedures are fragmented across States; reform needs a Union-led inter-governmental initiative with States and Law Commission consultation.
evidence: Court flagged fragmented state procedures and urged Union to lead an inter-governmental initiative with participation of States.

description: Researcher alleged earlier Digi Yatra app versions sent passenger data to developer Dataevolve's AWS servers and could access wide device data.
evidence: Investigation found past app versions sent passenger data to Dataevolve's AWS servers; app alleged to access 'all the data' on device.

description: Alleged retention of references to the original developer (Dataevolve) after it was replaced, reported in a 2024 investigation; a Delhi HC dispute over platform IP followed.
evidence: Delhi High Court examining ownership claims between Digi Yatra Foundation and Data Evolve Solutions over platform intellectual property.

description: System is run by the private Digi Yatra Foundation, which the Ministry says is outside RTI, raising accountability and ownership questions.
evidence: Ministry said Digi Yatra is not under RTI because the foundation is a private entity; questions on why it operates the system.

description: International extension excludes immigration steps, which need separate regulatory approvals and multi-stakeholder coordination; Kerala HC notice on alleged data misuse under DPDP rules.
evidence: Pilots do not include immigration, needing separate regulatory approvals; Kerala HC issued notice on alleged unauthorised passenger-data sharing.

description: Marketplace had a tepid start with only 23 farmers registered at launch before uptake grew.
evidence: After a tepid launch earlier in 2019, platform has about 30,000 farmers versus just 23 at launch.
